title: Abua Swasthya Card Jharkhand: Rs 15 Lakh Free Health
meta_description: Mukhyamantri Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana gives Jharkhand ration card holders Rs 15 lakh free health cover. Apply at bis.jharkhand.gov.in via Aadhaar.

hero.one_liner: Abua Swasthya Card gives Jharkhand ration card holders Rs 15 lakh free cashless treatment a year. For families not covered by Ayushman Bharat.

what_is_it: Mukhyamantri Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana (MASSY) is Jharkhand's flagship health insurance scheme, providing cashless medical treatment of up to Rs 15 lakh per family per year at government and empaneled private hospitals. The scheme is commonly known as the Abua Swasthya Card, and the Beneficiary Identification System (BIS) portal for enrollment is at bis.jharkhand.gov.in.

The scheme is open to all Jharkhand residents who hold a valid ration card (Green, Pink, or Yellow) issued by the state government or under the National Food Security Act. Existing beneficiaries of the central Ayushman Bharat PM-JAY scheme are also eligible to apply for the Abua Swasthya Card, which provides coverage significantly higher than the Rs 5 lakh ceiling under PM-JAY.

how_to_apply.title: Check eligibility
how_to_apply.description: Confirm that you hold a valid Green, Pink, or Yellow ration card issued by the Jharkhand government or under the NFSA; all family members listed on the ration card are covered. Have your Aadhaar card and Aadhaar-linked mobile number ready for enrollment.

how_to_apply.title: Visit BIS portal or enrollment point
how_to_apply.description: Go to bis.jharkhand.gov.in on your smartphone or computer, or visit a nearby Common Service Centre (CSC), Gram Panchayat office, or empaneled hospital. Select 'Beneficiary Login' and enter your Aadhaar-linked mobile number to begin the enrollment process.

how_to_apply.title: Complete Aadhaar Face RD authentication
how_to_apply.description: The enrollment system uses the Aadhaar Face RD app to capture a live photograph of the applicant and verify it against the Aadhaar database; no fingerprint device is required. Allow the camera to capture your face clearly in good lighting, as the verification completes almost instantly upon a successful match.

how_to_apply.title: Download the Abua Swasthya Card (PDF)
how_to_apply.description: Once face authentication succeeds, the Abua Swasthya Card is generated as a downloadable PDF with your name, family ID, and a QR code. Save the card on your phone or print a physical copy to present at empaneled hospitals for cashless treatment.

how_to_apply.title: Use the card for cashless treatment
how_to_apply.description: Present your Abua Swasthya Card or Aadhaar number at the Ayushman Bharat desk of any empaneled government or private hospital. The hospital will verify your eligibility on the BIS system and proceed with cashless admission without any upfront payment from you.

ministry: Department of Health, Medical Education and Family Welfare, Jharkhand

extra_sections.heading: What the Abua Swasthya Card Is
content: The Rs 15 lakh annual health cover applies to the entire family on a floater basis, meaning all household members together can claim up to Rs 15 lakh in a given year. There is no cap on family size, so larger families with many dependents are equally protected.

This is especially relevant for Jharkhand's tribal families, which often have multi-generational households living together under one roof. The scheme's universal family coverage ensures that even a large household of ten or twelve members collectively enjoys the full Rs 15 lakh benefit without any per-head reduction.

Pre-existing diseases are covered from day one of the scheme, meaning a beneficiary does not need to wait through any waiting period before claiming treatment for a condition they already had. This is a critical feature for a population where many elderly residents and persons with disabilities have chronic conditions such as diabetes, hypertension, or tuberculosis requiring expensive ongoing treatment.

The hospital network under Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana includes all government hospitals in Jharkhand as well as private hospitals that have been empaneled (registered) with the scheme. Since the scheme is linked to the national PM-JAY network, it also offers portability: Jharkhand beneficiaries can access empaneled hospitals in other states when they travel or migrate for work.

extra_sections.heading: Who Is Eligible
content: The Abua Swasthya Card is generated digitally as a PDF document through the BIS portal (bis.jharkhand.gov.in). The enrollment process uses Aadhaar Face RD (Registered Device) technology, where a live photograph of the applicant is captured via a camera-enabled device and matched against their Aadhaar biometric data for instant verification and card generation.

The shift to Aadhaar Face RD verification for the Abua Swasthya Card (updated in 2026) replaced the earlier slower document upload process, reducing enrollment time from days to minutes. Where previously beneficiaries had to upload scanned documents that were manually reviewed, the face-authentication system generates the card almost immediately upon successful identity verification.

To initiate enrollment, beneficiaries should visit the BIS portal at bis.jharkhand.gov.in or approach a Common Service Centre (CSC), Gram Panchayat office, or an empaneled hospital. At the enrollment point, the beneficiary logs in using their Aadhaar-linked mobile number, completes the face authentication, and receives the Abua Swasthya Card as a downloadable PDF.

The card contains the beneficiary's name, family ID, and a QR code for hospital verification. This QR code allows the hospital's system to instantly pull up the beneficiary's enrollment details and remaining annual limit at the time of admission.

extra_sections.title: How the Rs 15 Lakh Works
extra_sections.content:
The first Rs 5 lakh comes from the central PM-JAY scheme. The Jharkhand government tops this up so the total cover reaches Rs 15 lakh a family a year.

It is meant for families who do not get Ayushman Bharat, giving them free, cashless treatment at government and empanelled hospitals.

extra_sections.heading: The Ration Card Rule
content: The scheme covers a wide range of medical treatments including hospitalisation for surgeries, chemotherapy for cancer, dialysis for kidney disease, cardiac procedures, orthopaedic treatments, neonatal care, organ transplants, and emergency care. Over 1,500 treatment packages are defined under the PM-JAY network that forms the backbone of Abua Swasthya, covering both routine and complex procedures across specialties.

Cashless treatment works as follows: the beneficiary presents their Abua Swasthya Card (or Aadhaar number) at the empaneled hospital's Ayushman Bharat desk, the hospital verifies eligibility through the BIS system, and creates a pre-authorisation request before the patient is admitted. The hospital then claims the treatment cost from the scheme administrator after discharge, without the patient paying anything upfront.

The Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana does not require the beneficiary to pay any premium, enrolment fee, or co-payment. It is entirely free for eligible ration card holders, funded from the Jharkhand state budget.

This complete absence of any cost distinguishes it from contributory health insurance products and makes it accessible to the poorest households who cannot afford any upfront payment, even a nominal one. For daily wage earners and marginal farmers in Jharkhand's interior districts, even a few hundred rupees as a co-payment would be a genuine barrier to seeking timely medical care.

extra_sections.heading: How to Get the Card
content: Emergency hospitalisation under Abua Swasthya follows a simplified process: in genuine emergencies, the hospital admits the patient first and completes the verification formalities within 24 hours. This ensures that a beneficiary who arrives unconscious or in a critical state at an empaneled hospital is not turned away for want of on-the-spot card presentation.

The scheme covers 3 days of pre-hospitalisation costs (diagnostic tests and medicines taken before admission) and 15 days of post-discharge costs (medicines and follow-up tests recommended after hospital discharge) as part of the treatment package. This end-to-end coverage significantly reduces the out-of-pocket expenditure that families typically face in the period surrounding hospitalisation.

Jharkhand has a significant burden of diseases linked to its industrial, mining, and tribal demographic profile. Conditions such as silicosis from coal and mica mining, nutritional anaemia, sickle cell disease prevalent among certain tribal groups, vector-borne diseases like malaria and kala-azar, and tuberculosis are especially common, and the Abua Swasthya Card covers all these conditions under the defined national treatment packages.

The Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana supplements PM-JAY for Jharkhand beneficiaries by raising the annual ceiling from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 15 lakh. It also extends coverage to ration card holders who were not captured in the SECC 2011 database used for PM-JAY eligibility, thereby closing a significant exclusion gap in the state.

extra_sections.heading: What the Cover Includes
content: Beneficiaries who have been registered under PM-JAY can use the same PM-JAY card or Aadhaar number at empaneled hospitals, and the Abua Swasthya Card effectively upgrades their ceiling. Once the Rs 5 lakh PM-JAY limit is exhausted, the remaining Rs 10 lakh under the state scheme becomes available, giving combined coverage of up to Rs 15 lakh for qualifying beneficiaries.

The Beneficiary Identification System (BIS) portal at bis.jharkhand.gov.in is the central hub for all Abua Swasthya-related transactions including enrollment, card download, hospital empanelment queries, and beneficiary status checks. Beneficiaries who wish to verify whether they are already enrolled can enter their Aadhaar number on the portal to check their registration status.

Family members covered under the Abua Swasthya Card are all those listed in the ration card at the time of enrollment. If a new member joins the family, such as a newborn or a daughter-in-law, the family should first update their ration card and then request a BIS enrollment update to include the new member.

Empaneled hospitals can assist with BIS enrollment updates at the patient service desk, making it convenient for families who discover a coverage gap at the time of hospitalisation. The Jharkhand government has conducted outreach drives through ASHA workers and Gram Sabha meetings to ensure that maximum eligible households complete their Abua Swasthya Card enrollment before a medical emergency arises.

extra_sections.heading: If Your Name Is Missing
content: The scheme's name contains the word Abua, which means 'our own' in the Mundari tribal language, and is the same prefix used in Abua Awas Yojana (housing). This consistent Abua branding signals the state government's positioning of these programmes as Jharkhand's own initiatives tailored for its tribal and economically marginalised population.

The Jharkhand government has set up a grievance redressal mechanism for Abua Swasthya beneficiaries who face issues such as hospital denial, card generation failure, or disputes over treatment packages. Complaints can be filed through the BIS portal or at the district health office, and the scheme guidelines mandate a time-bound resolution process.

Even in cases where an empaneled private hospital initially refuses to provide cashless treatment, the beneficiary has the right to approach the district nodal officer (DNO) for the PM-JAY/Abua scheme who can intervene and direct the hospital to honour the entitlement. This redressal pathway is important in a state like Jharkhand where beneficiaries in remote areas may face resistance from private facilities that prefer cash-paying patients.

The long-term vision of the Mukhyamantri Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana is to ensure that no Jharkhand family falls into poverty because of a catastrophic illness or medical emergency. Catastrophic health expenditure has historically been one of the leading drivers of household debt among rural families in India, and schemes like Abua Swasthya are specifically designed to eliminate this financial risk for the lowest-income households in the state.

extra_sections.title: Pre-existing Diseases Covered
extra_sections.desc:
Unlike many private health policies, this scheme covers pre-existing diseases from the day you enrol.

There is no waiting period, so an already-ill family member can get cashless treatment as soon as the card is active.

extra_sections.heading: Abua Swasthya vs Ayushman Bharat
content: Beneficiaries of Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana should keep their ration card updated and ensure that the ration card number is correctly linked to their Aadhaar on the BIS portal. Any mismatch between the ration card database and the Aadhaar records can delay card generation, and beneficiaries facing such issues should visit their local Panchayat Sevak or Block Development Office for assistance with the correction.

The scheme also provides secondary and tertiary care benefits, which means it covers not just district hospital admissions but also treatment at specialised medical colleges and super-specialty hospitals empaneled under the PM-JAY network. For conditions requiring highly specialised care such as open heart surgery, liver transplant, or bone marrow transplant, beneficiaries from even the remotest parts of Jharkhand can access treatment at major urban hospitals without bearing any cost.

Ayushman Mitra are trained staff deployed at empaneled hospitals under the PM-JAY network to help beneficiaries navigate the admission and claim process. In Jharkhand, these Ayushman Mitra also assist with Abua Swasthya Card-related queries, and their presence at the hospital helps first-time beneficiaries who may be unfamiliar with the cashless process complete their paperwork smoothly.

The connection between Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana and the Abua Awas Yojana (housing scheme) and Mukhyamantri Maiya Samman Yojana (monthly cash to women) reflects Jharkhand's integrated approach to welfare for its poor households. Together, these three Abua-brand schemes address the three most critical vulnerability dimensions for low-income families: housing insecurity, income insufficiency, and health expenditure risk.

extra_sections.heading: Why the Card Matters
content: Beneficiaries seeking mental health treatment may also access care under the Abua Swasthya scheme, as certain mental health conditions and related hospitalisation packages are included under the PM-JAY framework. The National Mental Health Programme (NMHP) services at government hospitals are available to Abua Swasthya cardholders, including outpatient mental health consultations and inpatient psychiatric care where required.

For beneficiaries who have been denied treatment at an empaneled hospital or who have received a bill for services that should have been cashless, the Jharkhand State Health Agency (SHA) operates a helpline and a web-based complaint portal. Reporting such incidents promptly is important both to recover costs where applicable and to ensure that hospitals which repeatedly violate the scheme's cashless mandate face action under the empanelment agreement.

extra_sections.title: For Families Left Out of Ayushman Bharat
extra_sections.content:
The scheme is built mainly for Jharkhand families who did not get an Ayushman Bharat card. It fills that gap and raises the cover to Rs 15 lakh.

If you already have Ayushman Bharat, you still benefit, since the state top-up extends your cover well beyond the central Rs 5 lakh.

extra_sections.heading: Why the Card Matters More
content: The state government periodically conducts verification drives to remove ineligible or duplicate enrollments from the BIS database, ensuring that the scheme's benefits are accurately targeted to genuine ration card holders. Beneficiaries who have recently changed their address, updated their ration card, or received a new ration card should re-verify their enrollment status on the BIS portal to confirm that their Abua Swasthya Card details are current and accurate.

Women are especially encouraged to complete the Abua Swasthya Card enrollment for their entire household, as they are often the primary caregivers who arrange medical treatment when family members fall ill. Since women are typically the ones who accompany sick children, elderly parents, or disabled relatives to hospital, having a valid Abua Swasthya Card readily available on their phone ensures they can initiate cashless admission without delay.

extra_sections.heading: Keeping the Card Active
content: The Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana also covers maternal and neonatal care packages, which is particularly significant for Jharkhand where maternal mortality and infant mortality rates remain higher than the national average in some districts. Institutional delivery at empaneled hospitals under the Abua Swasthya scheme is covered as part of the maternity care package, encouraging more women to opt for safe delivery in a hospital setting rather than at home.

Elderly beneficiaries aged 70 and above who are also entitled to coverage under the expanded Ayushman Bharat Vaya Vandana Yojana (AB-PMJAY for senior citizens) receive an additional benefit layer on top of the Abua Swasthya cover. The convergence of these central and state schemes means that senior citizens from Jharkhand's poorest families can access among the highest levels of publicly funded health protection in India.

extra_sections.heading: Keeping the Card Active More
content: The state health department periodically publishes district-wise and hospital-wise claim settlement data for the Abua Swasthya scheme to promote transparency and allow civil society to monitor whether funds are flowing to beneficiaries as intended. Beneficiaries and advocacy groups can use this data to identify districts where claim rejection rates are unusually high or where hospitals are not honouring the cashless mandate, and bring such patterns to the attention of the district administration.

District hospitals and community health centres in Jharkhand display the list of covered treatments and the Abua Swasthya Card enrollment process prominently at their outpatient departments. For beneficiaries who do not have access to a smartphone or cannot complete the online process independently, hospital staff and Ayushman Mitra at the Ayushman Bharat desk are authorised to complete the enrollment on their behalf using the Aadhaar Face RD verification at the facility.

faqs.question: What is Mukhyamantri Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana?
faqs.answer:
Mukhyamantri Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana is Jharkhand's health insurance scheme that provides Rs 15 lakh per family per year for cashless treatment at government and empaneled private hospitals. It is open to all Jharkhand ration card holders (Green, Pink, Yellow) and existing PM-JAY beneficiaries.

The BIS portal is at bis.jharkhand.gov.in.

faqs.question: How much health cover does the Abua Swasthya Card give?
faqs.answer: Rs 15 lakh per family per year on a floater basis, meaning all household members together can claim up to Rs 15 lakh. This is three times the Rs 5 lakh cover under PM-JAY and applies cashlessly at government and empaneled private hospitals.

faqs.question: Who is eligible for the Abua Swasthya Card?
faqs.answer:
All Jharkhand residents holding a valid Green, Pink, or Yellow ration card issued by the state or under the NFSA are eligible. PM-JAY beneficiaries in Jharkhand are also eligible.

There is no separate income ceiling or BPL card requirement beyond ration card possession.

faqs.question: How do I apply for the Abua Swasthya Card?
faqs.answer:
Visit bis.jharkhand.gov.in or a nearby CSC, Gram Panchayat, or empaneled hospital. Log in with your Aadhaar-linked mobile number, complete the Aadhaar Face RD live photo verification, and download your Abua Swasthya Card as a PDF.

No fingerprint device or physical form is needed.

faqs.question: Is the Abua Swasthya Card free?
faqs.answer:
Yes. There is no premium, enrolment fee, or co-payment.

The scheme is completely free for eligible Jharkhand ration card holders, funded entirely from the state budget.

faqs.question: Are pre-existing diseases covered under Abua Swasthya?
faqs.answer:
Yes. Pre-existing diseases are covered from day one of enrollment, with no waiting period.

Conditions like diabetes, hypertension, or tuberculosis that the beneficiary had before getting the card are covered immediately from the date of enrollment.

faqs.question: What hospitals can I use with the Abua Swasthya Card?
faqs.answer: All government hospitals in Jharkhand and private hospitals empaneled under the PM-JAY / Ayushman Bharat network. Due to national portability, the card can also be used at empaneled hospitals in other states across India.

faqs.question: What is covered under the Abua Swasthya Suraksha Yojana?
faqs.answer: All hospitalisation costs for surgeries, chemotherapy, dialysis, cardiac procedures, orthopaedic treatments, neonatal care, organ transplants, emergency care, and over 1,500 defined medical packages. It also covers 3 days of pre-hospitalisation and 15 days post-discharge costs.

faqs.question: Does Abua Swasthya Card cover all family members?
faqs.answer:
Yes. All household members listed on the ration card are covered under the Rs 15 lakh annual floater limit.

There is no cap on family size, so even large multi-generational households are fully covered.

faqs.question: I already have PM-JAY. Do I still need the Abua Swasthya Card?
faqs.answer:
Yes, you should still enroll. For PM-JAY beneficiaries in Jharkhand, the Abua Card upgrades the annual cover from Rs 5 lakh to Rs 15 lakh.

Once the PM-JAY ceiling is exhausted, the state Abua scheme covers additional costs up to the combined Rs 15 lakh total.
